questions.q: Cyclohexene is treated with CH₂I₂ and a zinc–copper couple in ether. The product is:
questions.explain: The carbenoid ICH₂ZnI delivers a CH₂ across the C=C, giving a cyclopropane fused to the ring, with ZnI₂ as by-product.

questions.q: trans-But-2-ene reacts with CH₂I₂/Zn(Cu). The product is:
options: A mixture of cis and trans isomers
questions.explain: The CH₂ is transferred to both carbons at once on the same face (syn, stereospecific), so alkene geometry is kept.

questions.q: Which statement about the Simmons–Smith reagent is correct?
options: It is a carbenoid, ICH₂ZnI, that gives no C–H insertion side products
It adds in two steps through a carbocation
questions.explain: ICH₂ZnI behaves like singlet methylene in concerted addition but, unlike free :CH₂, does not give C–H insertion products; dichlorocyclopropanes come from :CCl₂.

questions.q: Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol is treated with CH₂I₂ and Zn(Cu). On which face of the ring is the new CH₂ delivered?
options: The face trans to the OH, because it is less hindered
Both faces equally, giving a racemic mixture of diastereomers
No reaction occurs because OH destroys the reagent
The face cis to the OH, because zinc coordinates to the hydroxyl group
questions.explain: In allylic alcohols the zinc binds the OH and directs the CH₂ to the same face, even when that face is more crowded; steric control applies only without a directing group.
